clue.text: Boatman might be on quarterdeck keeping watch by one

indicators.note: the stern position holds the other pieces within it, as a ship keeps its crew

parts.note: the quarterdeck is at the stern of a ship, so something on it is aft
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or watch
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A sailor stands on the quarterdeck, keeping watch beside a shipmate.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is also this puzzle's setter, so the definition is a joke on his name. This clue was missing from the printed paper and supplied later.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works boats is often floating on water, which is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: 12 15 achievement — bird seen to fly on soft wings

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the long phrase about acting selfishly, here meaning to enrich oneself

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: a feat is an achievement
a heron is a wading bird

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered into a new order
the wings of a word are its outer letters, here of soft

explanation.surface: A bird takes to the air on soft wings, a fine achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fly' rearranges SEEN as ESNE; 'on' puts it above ST, the outside letters of 'soft', in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathering your nest means enriching yourself at others' expense, a classic way of putting yourself first.

clue.text: Heart moved to take top job and get gold

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is shifted so that it takes the first position

parts.note: a chore is a job, usually a tedious one

explanation.surface: Someone moves their heart to take the top job and wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of CHORE is its middle letter O; moving it to the top (the front) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown pigment, so it names a golden colour.

clue.text: Rust-proofed with poor quality paint and let down

indicators.note: work of poor quality is botched, so these words come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Something was rust-proofed with cheap paint and it let the owner down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor quality' is the anagram signal: it looks like it describes the paint, but it tells you to jumble two words of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating iron or steel with a thin layer of tin protects it from corrosion.

clue.text: Bullies exploit what we give to our children

definitions.text: what we give to our children

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them, so bullies means cows
to milk a situation is to exploit it

explanation.surface: Bullies take advantage, and something is handed to our children.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullies also suggests bulls, a misleading nod to cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy produced by cattle is the usual drink given to youngsters.

clue.text: Outline of your body, comme le dit Spooner?

indicators.note: French for as Spooner says it, so the start sounds of two French words are swapped

parts.note: ton is French for your
corps is French for body

explanation.surface: An outline of your body, as Spooner might put it in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton corps (your body) swaps its opening sounds to give con tor, which sounds like the answer; the French in the clue signals the French words.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is the shape or outline of something, such as a figure or a landscape.

clue.text: Permitted to crow about being eccentric

indicators.note: turning about means the words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OK means allowed or permitted
to caw is to make a crow's cry

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to boast about being odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns both pieces round as one unit, so the crow's cry comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is slang for crazy or very odd, the same as eccentric.

clue.text: Grommet fails in old car

indicators.note: a part that fails breaks down, so the word's letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A grommet gives way in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: The MG Metro was a sporty version of the Austin Metro, a British small car of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a specific vintage British hatchback model, so an example of an old motor.

clue.text: Policy a psychologist set out to 12 15

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the long phrase about acting selfishly, here meaning to enrich oneself

parts.note: a party line is its policy
a means one
Benjamin Spock was an American paediatrician famous for child psychology

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A psychologist sets out a policy for putting yourself first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining your pockets means making money for yourself, often dishonestly, which is selfish behaviour.

clue.text: Make money by the hour in gambling den with bridge player

indicators.note: the hour is placed in the gambling den

parts.note: a casino is a gambling house
h is the abbreviation for hour
the four bridge players are named by compass points, one being North, N

explanation.surface: Someone earns hourly in a casino alongside a bridge partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in on something is to profit from it.

clue.text: Stick together to make money? Self-centred

indicators.note: the self word is put at the centre of the money word

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a small amount of money
me is the self

explanation.surface: A self-centred person sticks together to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word 'Self-centred' does two jobs: its first half gives the pronoun and its second half says where to put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement as a verb means to bind or join firmly.

clue.text: Role of selfishness in this puzzle maybe initially lost for old solver

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word goes missing

parts.words: Role of selfishness in this puzzle
parts.note: selfishness is the puzzle's subject, its theme

explanation.surface: The part played by selfishness in this puzzle is lost on an old solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is the person addressed: you, which in old English is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic object form of you, the person doing the solving.

clue.text: Act selfishly to make fortune, outrageously less sensitive (nothing inside?) after semblance of love

indicators.note: the fortune piece comes after the semblance of love

parts.note: a look is an appearance or semblance
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the numb and nothing pieces are placed within the rearranged letters
outrageously suggests wild treatment, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: numbed means less sensitive, as more numb
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: To make a fortune, one behaves outrageously and callously, with nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' jumbles the word fortune; 'inside' puts the less-sensitive word and the zero within that jumble; 'after' places all of it behind the semblance and love pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to put your own interests first, which is acting selfishly.

clue.text: Could it be Mohammed said to make a killing?

indicators.note: said shows the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: Mohammed is the Prophet of Islam

explanation.surface: Could Mohammed be said to have killed someone?
explanation.definitionFit: Making a killing means earning a large gain, which is what profiting does.

clue.text: Redeemed, made amends or converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinner was redeemed, made amends, or converted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom a captive is to pay to free them, which is to redeem them.

clue.text: See 12
"Bigoted, snide, perverse" in dictionary

indicators.note: the rearranged word is placed in the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: perverse means turned awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry defines bigoted, snide and perverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided view is partial and prejudiced, much like a bigoted one.

clue.text: Conspicuously selfish, utterly blind

indicators.note: the answer sits plainly in view inside the next words

explanation.surface: Someone conspicuously selfish is utterly blind to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a hinged cover for a window, a kind of window blind.

clue.text: Kill doctor, stabbed with uniform's fastening

parts.note: to do in is to kill

indicators.note: the doctor is pierced by the uniform letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doctor is killed, stabbed with something from a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing up buttons or a zip is fastening them.

clue.text: Mistakes note on unknown vessels, missing cable's header

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
x is the classic unknown in algebra

indicators.note: the first letter of cable is dropped

parts.note: cups are drinking vessels

explanation.surface: A note on unknown ships is wrong, the cable's header missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mix-ups are confusions or errors.

clue.text: Mast's up with difficulty? Boatman's apt to take it for granted

definitions.text: apt to take it for granted

indicators.note: a mast going up with difficulty is in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive here supplies its S as a letter
Boatman is the setter, so Boatman's is I have, shortened

explanation.surface: Is getting the mast up hard? Boatman assumes it will be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges MASTSUP as ASSUMPT; Boatman's stands for I've, the setter saying I have.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumptive describes someone inclined to presume or take things for granted.

clue.text: Sit and solve selfless cipher

indicators.note: solving a cipher means unscrambling it, so the letters are rearranged
without the self, the letter I standing for me is removed

explanation.surface: Sit down and crack a code without thinking of yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'selfless' removes I (the self) from CIPHER, and 'solve' rearranges the remaining CPHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird perches when it sits on a branch.

clue.text: As one might be, following tips resulting in cash hoarding

indicators.note: the tips of the words that follow are their first letters

explanation.surface: Following tips and hoarding cash, a person ends up wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: One is number one, the theme's self, who may well be wealthy from looking after himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hoards money is wealthy, as the selfish number one might be.

clue.text: Stick at nothing to take ultimate prize in western show

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of prize

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone will stick at nothing to win the top prize at a western show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a cowboy exhibition of riding and roping from the American West.

clue.text: Self-absorbed, into prophet, an abstemious one

indicators.note: the abstainer is taken in by the prophet, so it goes inside

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
TT means teetotal, an abstainer from alcohol

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed teetotaller is taken in by a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter often refers to himself, so the setter is the self here.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a puzzle speaks as I or me in clues, the self of the puzzle.

clue.text: Try to take too much and exploit selfless act?

parts.note: to have a go is to try
OD means overdose, to take too much
an exploit is a deed

explanation.surface: Someone tries to take too much and exploit a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A good deed is an act of kindness, done for others rather than oneself.

clue.text: Was that Elvis's pelvis? It's seen moving across the galaxy

definitions.text: It's seen moving across the galaxy

parts.note: Elvis was a star, so his pelvis is a star's
the hip is the pelvic region

explanation.surface: Was that Elvis's famous swivelling pelvis seen crossing the galaxy?
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis Presley was nicknamed Elvis the Pelvis for his hip movements.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a spacecraft for interstellar travel.

clue.text: Me, me, selfish me, first and foremost?

definitions.text: Me, me, selfish me, first and foremost?

parts.note: the ego is the self, me
I is the subject form of me

indicators.note: the first letters of the words come foremost

explanation.surface: A self-centred person keeps putting me first and foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is selfishness, always putting oneself first, which the clue's chant describes.
